architectures.description: Chip generations. Matrix-format support is a property of the generation, so it is recorded once here and every unit that names this generation inherits it.

drives.description: Reference drives for lookup tables read from an SSD. The first listed is the default.

lines.description: The observation ledger: every measured number on the page, each inside the serving line that produced it. Nothing interpolated, extrapolated or modeled belongs here.

confidence.description: Human-readable gloss for each confidence code.

qualityIndex.description: The one quality measure the open-weight frontier is drawn with. Scores from other versions of it are kept but never compared with the current one.

attribution.description: The byline the source requires wherever its data is shown.

note.description: Known weaknesses of the measure, with evidence.

asOf.description: YYYY or YYYY-MM. A price without a date is not a fact.

pricing.description: Open by design: add lease/used/bundle alongside msrp and street without a schema change.

power.description: Draw for ONE unit, observed under LLM inference. Deliberately not hardware.tdpW: inference is bandwidth-bound and does not reach the datasheet ceiling, and cards are commonly power-capped. Build totals are summed from this, never stored.

catalogUnit.description: A purchasable piece of hardware -- the thing a datasheet describes. Lines and candidates are quantities of these, so a price or spec corrected here corrects everything containing it.

tdpW.description: Datasheet TDP. Recorded only; nothing derives from it -- see power.

values.description: Rated throughput keyed by precision (fp32, tf32, bf16, fp16, fp8, fp4, int8, ...). Suffix a key with ':sparse' for structured-sparsity figures, or ':vector' for a shader-ALU rate (packed FP16, dot-product INT8) on a card with no matrix units; vector rates prove no matrix path and bound prefill only when the card has none. New precisions need no schema change.

unofficial.description: Keys of values that are not the vendor's rating for this card: worked out from other figures, or taken from a third party. The note says which and how. The page marks them, and a ceiling resting on one says so.

formFactor.description: What the GPU physically is: an add-in card, a module for a vendor baseboard, Apple's MPX module for the Mac Pro (2019), or part of an SoC or APU.

slots.description: Slot width of an add-in card: 1, 2, 3 ...

hostLink.description: The GPU's PCIe link to the host CPU as the vendor rates it: generation and lanes. Per-direction throughput is derived from these. Left out for an integrated GPU, which has none.

peerLink.description: The largest group of these cards that can exchange data GPU to GPU without going through PCIe (NVLink, Infinity Fabric, Xe Link), on vendor-supported hardware: a bridge for an add-in card, the vendor's baseboard for an SXM or OAM module. 0 means the card has no such link. Left out, the card's link is not yet sourced.

options.description: Smaller supported group sizes, when there is more than one (a 2-way and a 4-way bridge, say).

fabric.description: What joins them: 'NVLink 3 bridge', 'NVLink 4 via NVSwitch (HGX)', 'Infinity Fabric Link bridge', 'Xe Link bridge' ...

topology.description: All-to-all (switched), pairs, ring or mesh, with link bandwidth where the vendor states it.

source.description: Where it is stated: a URL, then a verbatim quote.

board.description: Set when one board carries several GPUs that the host sees as separate devices (the A16's four). Memory, bandwidth, compute and links are then per GPU, and the price is per board.

source.description: Where it is stated: a URL, then a verbatim quote.

sources.description: Where this record's specifications came from. Required once any specification field is filled, so an unsourced number cannot land quietly.

note.description: Caveats — e.g. that a bandwidth figure is SoC-wide rather than a discrete card's.

arch.description: The chip generation (an architectures id). Matrix-format support is inherited from it.

short.description: A short name for chart labels.

formatOverrides.description: Where this card differs from its generation. Needs a note on the unit saying why.

composition.description: What this configuration is made of. Cost, power and capacity are summed from it; storing them directly is not allowed.

rig.description: The hardware a line ran on, or a candidate would run on: catalog units, how they are connected, and the host around them. Cost, power draw and capacity are derived from the units and never stored here.

interconnect.description: How the units talk to each other. Absent means nobody has looked; say so in a note rather than guessing a link type.

kind.description: nvlink, infinity-fabric, xe-link, pcie ... free text on purpose, so a new fabric needs no schema change.

linksPerGpu.description: Peer links on each GPU, counted the way the vendor counts them.

peakP2pGBsPerGpu.description: Peak theoretical GPU-to-GPU bandwidth per GPU, both directions summed over every link, as the vendor states it. A rating, not a measurement, and only as good as what the board actually wires; leave it out when the vendor does not state GB/s.

hostLinkGBs.description: Peak host link per GPU, both directions, line rate x lanes with encoding overhead not subtracted (the convention AMD uses for its PCIe figures). This is what a host-RAM-resident table or a KV spill tier streams over.

costUsd.description: Price of the bridge or carrier board itself, which belongs to no card, plus parts a carrier cannot run without (an SXM carrier's cables and heatsinks, say) when a note itemises them. Absent means unpriced, and a rig total that leaves it out says so. Zero is a real answer: some bridges ship with the cards.

costHighUsd.description: The top of the observed price range, when bridges have been seen at very different prices. The rig total then reads as a range.

p2p.description: Whether peer-to-peer transfers were actually enabled for the run. A container or VM can disable them without anyone noticing.

powerCapW.description: Per-unit power cap the run was under, if any.

carrier.description: Id of the carrier board the units mount on. The carrier supplies the bridge, peer wiring, host link, price and fit; the rig's own interconnect may then only add a note or p2p.

provenance.description: Where a number came from and whether the page's maintainer vouches for it. `kind` says what sort of source it is; `attestation` is the maintainer's own word, declared and never inferred. Who ran the test or compiled the data is deliberately not the question: a number is weighed by whether someone accountable saw it happen and whether its inputs can be checked.

kind.description: first-party = the maintainer's own measurement program; issue-report = a GitHub issue, PR or discussion; forum = Reddit, Level1Techs, vendor forums, Bilibili and the like; review = independent articles, benchmark sites and benchmark repositories; vendor = the hardware or software maker.

attestation.description: witnessed = the maintainer personally saw this hardware produce these numbers. reported = someone else's account, included because nothing gives a specific reason to doubt it; where there is a specific reason, leave the number out.

source.description: A repository path, issue or comment reference, or URL -- enough to go and read the original.

digest.description: sha256 of the manifest that pins the receipts, when one exists.

reproduced.description: Whether anyone other than the reporter has reproduced the numbers. Required for issue-report and forum sources.

linePoint.description: One number from one line. Depth, stream count and per-stream-versus-aggregate are always stated, because a bare tok/s means three different things without them.

depth.description: Context tokens per stream when the point was taken (for a cold prefill, the prompt length). null only when the source did not say, and then depthNote says what it did say.

basis.description: One stream is always per-stream; aggregate means the total across streams.

range.description: Low and high across repeated runs, when the source reports a range rather than one figure. Give exactly one of value or range.

confidence.description: m = measured, primary source; m~ = measured, secondary or anecdotal source. Nothing estimated belongs in the ledger.

spec.description: Whether speculative decoding was active for this point, when it differs from the line's default.

prefillBasis.description: Prefill only. cold = the whole prompt was evaluated; new-tokens = the rate over only the tokens not already cached.

acceptance.description: Draft acceptance, as the engine defines it. Not comparable across engines.

line.description: One serving line: a rig, an engine, a set of weights, a cache and the flags it ran with. Every reading belongs to exactly one, so none of those is ever implied by a table row.

model.description: A key in assets/models.js MODELS, or null when the source did not name the model (then modelNote says what it did say).

lineage.description: upstream, fork, vendor ... where the code comes from and who maintains it. Free text: specialist engines exist for most of this hardware.

format.description: As the source names it. "not recorded" is an honest value.

kld.description: KL divergence of the quantized model against a stated reference, on code and on prose. Quality, not speed: tok/s across different quants is not the same product.

key.description: The weight-format family in assets/ceiling.js WEIGHT_FORMATS, which decides the matrix precision and a typical bits-per-weight when bpw is not recorded.

kibPerToken.description: Measured KV cost per token on this engine. The config-derived figure is a lower bound on it (see tools/test-kv.mjs).

offload.description: Work that ran on hardware outside the unit's rated GPU figures: the Apple Neural Engine, the CPU. Readings of the metrics named are shown against the ceiling but not held to it, the way speculative decoding is.

tokens.description: The KV pool as loaded. Under a unified pool this is shared by every slot, not a per-request limit.

registryId.description: The Discipline substrate id, when the line is one.

admission.description: Discipline's own word, only where a registry entry carries one. Absent for lines that are characterization only.

status.description: withdrawn = the build or configuration is known to produce invalid numbers; say why in hazards.

parallel.description: How a multi-card rig split the model. Without it there is no single ceiling to compare against.

observed.description: When the source says the numbers were taken or published.

recorded.description: When the numbers entered this page -- the latest they could have been observed.

modelParams.description: Only for a line whose source named no model but gave its size ("a 27B dense model"). Gives a weights-only ceiling, which can only be higher than the true one.

candidate.description: A rig under consideration with no measured line yet.

sources.description: Where this rig's description came from, beyond its interconnect source: write-ups, reports, listings. Each entry starts with an https URL, optionally followed by ' -- ' and what it supports. The page shows them as links under the rig.

carrier.description: A board that GPU modules mount on (an SXM2 carrier, adapter or baseboard), or a whole system built around one (kind "system": a DGX, an HGX server, a Gaudi server): what it wires between its slots and to the host, what it costs, and which catalog units are known to work in it. Rigs name a carrier instead of repeating these facts, so every rig on one board shares one record.

kind.description: board (the default when absent): a carrier the owner fits into a host. system: a complete machine with its own CPU, memory, chassis and power, described in host.

socket.description: Module socket, matched against each unit's formFactor.name (SXM2, SXM4 ...).

peer.description: How the board joins its slots to each other. Absent means nobody has looked.

kind.description: nvlink; ethernet when accelerators meet over their own integrated RoCE ports wired on the board (Gaudi); or none when slots meet only over PCIe.

peakP2pGBsPerGpu.description: Peak GPU-to-GPU bandwidth per GPU, both directions summed over every link, as a vendor or write-up states it. A rating, not a measurement.

switch.description: Whether a PCIe switch sits between the slots and the host. With one, PCIe peer traffic between GPUs on the same switch stays off the host. Absent means not recorded.

hostLink.description: The board's PCIe uplinks. The page derives each GPU's host link as line rate x lanes, both directions, divided among the GPUs sharing an uplink, encoding overhead not subtracted. Absent means not recorded.

gpusPerUplink.description: GPUs sharing one uplink when all of them stream.

attach.description: What the host needs: slots, cables, risers, adapter cards.

maxW.description: The maker's maximum draw for the whole system.

pricing.description: The board's or system's own price. Absent means unpriced, and a rig total that leaves it out says so.

includes.description: What the price buys: the board alone, or the board with cables, a host card, water blocks ...

modules.description: Modules the price already includes, so a rig on this carrier does not pay for them again. Absent means none.

parts.description: Parts the board cannot run without that its price leaves out (host cables, an enclosure and supply), summed into rig totals. Cooling that depends on the module stays in notes.

fits.description: Which catalog units work in the board, and how their peers meet on it. verified: an owner ran it and said so, or the maker sells or supports the system with it installed; reported: a seller or second-hand claim, or a maker's claim for a bare board; untested: nobody has said either way; fails: reported not to work.

peer.description: How this unit's peers meet on this board: nvlink or ethernet only when both the board and the module wire it.

host.description: A system's own host: required when kind is system, not allowed otherwise.

cpu.description: The host processors, or what stands in for them (an external host on cables).

memoryGB.description: Host memory as the maker ships it.

memoryMaxGB.description: The most host memory the maker says it takes.

chassis.description: Rack units or tower, and anything about size, weight or noise that decides where it can live.

openModel.description: An open-weight model tracked for the size frontier: its size from its own repository, and its scores on the quality index. The page derives which models are on the frontier.

model.description: Id of the model's shape in MODELS (assets/models.js), when it has one.

active.description: Parameters used per token; equal to total for a dense model, absent when the card does not say.

source.description: Where the counts come from, with the card's own words.

lookup.description: Parameters in lookup tables (n-gram embeddings, Engram memory) that the total includes. They are read a few rows per token, so the page places them in host RAM and leaves them out of GPU memory.

lookupBits.description: Bits per lookup-table parameter as the checkpoint ships them. Absent: precision not recorded, and the page gives no host-RAM figure.

mtp.description: Parameters in the checkpoint's MTP head; 0 when the checkpoint was checked and carries none. Resident only when speculative decoding uses it.

mtpInTotal.description: Whether the published total already includes the MTP head.

split.description: Where lookup and mtp were counted: the card's words, or the checkpoint's safetensors headers at a revision.

precision.description: As released: BF16, FP8, MXFP4 experts with BF16 elsewhere ...

sizeGB.description: The repository's size as Hugging Face shows it.

variant.description: The source's name for the setting scored (an effort level, a reasoning mode).

formatState.description: native = the matrix units take this input type; absent = they do not (emulation or upcasting does not count); unknown = no source found either way.

architecture.description: One chip generation and what its matrix units (tensor cores, MFMA, WMMA, XMX) can multiply.

matrixUnits.description: What the vendor calls the matrix hardware, or a statement that there is none.

sources.description: Where the classification comes from. Every native or absent state must be named by some source's `supports` list ("fp8" for native, "fp8:absent" for absent); a state no source supports is "unknown".

locator.description: Where in the source the quote sits.

short.description: The label on the setting's chip.

capacityGB.description: The capacity the figures are for; random-read rates differ by capacity.

latencyUs.description: Average 4 KiB random-read latency at queue depth 1, one thread, as measured: the figure the page uses. Measured rather than the maker's, because most makers state none and those that do state faster ones.

setup.description: The tool, operating system and test PC.

qd1Iops.description: The maker's queue-depth-1 random-read IOPS, where it states one. Shown for comparison, not used.

makerLatencyUs.description: The maker's stated read latency (an upper bound such as "<10 µs"), where it gives one. Shown for comparison, not used.

peakAt.description: Queue depth and threads the peak was stated at, or that they were not.

source.description: The maker's datasheet or brochure; a third-party copy is named as such in the note.
